cleared.check: Task 2. What a wrong word at SqrtPriceMath.sol:52, :97 or :105 could change.
cleared.result: Nothing that is committed. Line 97 runs in the step that exhausts the input (SwapMath.sol:76-82) with amountIn = amountRemainingLessFee > 2^160, and line 105 in the exact-output step that stops short with amountOut = amountRemaining > 2^160 (SwapMath.sol:94-98). The loop then ends with the specified-currency delta above 2^160, and Pool.sol:455 or :459 reverts at toInt128 whatever price the step computed. All 24 line 52 cases, the 3 line 97 cases and the 9 line 105 cases end in SafeCastOverflow (0x93dafdf1) in the interpreter, in native code at both tags and in pyevm.py. Cycle 25 showed that line 52 is reached only with more than about 2^160 units of currency1 in range and that every such swap reverts the same way. A native fault in these blocks could change gas or revert data of a reverted swap, never a payout.

cleared.check: Task 2. cleared.result: The fee growth words, fees owed and storage after every transaction are equal in the interpreter, native code at both tags and pyevm.py. Where the owed fees exceed int128 the poke and the removal revert with SafeCastOverflow in all three; that is the known behaviour of F-005 (actor pool-creator, a donor must give away more than 2^127 units) and not a difference between engines.

cleared.check: Can the comparison of this cycle fail?
cleared.result: Yes. Flipping one bit of a PoolManager storage word or of an output word in the reference is reported, and flipping each 32-byte word of a driver output in turn is reported for 22 of 30 words; the other eight are the driver's own two token balances, which differ by construction, and ABI header or padding words. The harness itself compares the full dump of both engines (trace, storage, transient storage, balances, token balances, logs, gas).

leadResults.answer: The native blocks of SqrtPriceMath.sol:52 (0x5d5d, 0x5d6c, 0x5d71), :97 (0x503a, 0x505c and the mulDiv copy 0x588a, 0x58d6, 0x58db), :105 (0x519c, 0x51cf, 0x51e4 and the general mulDiv 0x5943 to 0x59da) and Position.sol:94-96 (0x173e, 0x1755 and the Q128 mulDiv copy 0x5703, 0x5752, 0x5757, 0x577c) were all entered in native code by cycle 25 and 27 cases before this cycle; only 0x593c was not, and it cannot be reached because line 97 implies prod1 >= 1. Rerun with the rebuilt harness, the 37 entering cases give the same words in the interpreter, native code at both tags and pyevm.py, and six new fee scenarios with an observable 512-bit result agree too. Every swap through lines 52, 97 and 105 reverts at Pool.sol:455-459, so a wrong word there cannot reach committed state.

The 37 changed and unentered blocks are named in out/summary.json: 12 decode arguments, 20 compute inside extsload(bytes32[]), exttload(bytes32[]), extsload(bytes32,uint256), supportsInterface, transferOwnership, setProtocolFee and collectProtocolFees, and 5 cannot be reached (0x3aae, 0x40d7, 0x593c, 0x5b2e, 0x5bd5). The cycle 28 scenarios enter all 32 reachable ones at v0.16.5 and v0.16.7, with identical interpreter and native dumps and the pyevm.py words and storage. 0x40d7 (literal shifted by a computed count) only builds revert data for hook calldata shorter than 4 bytes, which the code never produces; 0xed4 and 0x593c have been read above; 0x2f7b to 0x2fe7 is the bytes32[] calldata decoder, entered with well formed and malformed arrays.
